description: An underwriting manager must decide whether to grant a temporary debt-service covenant waiver to a property company and finalize the waiver period, liquidity protection, equity support, and monitoring conditions, with input from risk, legal, and relationship management.

shared_context.S1: The property company has an $8,000,000 term loan with a minimum debt-service coverage ratio of 1.20.
shared_context.S2: The latest reported ratio is 1.16 after a one-time inventory write-down, and the borrower is requesting a 120-day waiver.
shared_context.S3: The borrower has otherwise made all scheduled payments, and the loan is not currently past due.
shared_context.S4: Mara makes the binding waiver decision; under the bank's routine review process, she asks risk, legal, and relationship management for relevant information before finalizing the waiver.
shared_context.S5: Any approved waiver is recorded in a written amendment and circulated to the borrower and servicing team.

PF1.text: Elias completed an updated stress test this morning that permits a waiver only if the borrower maintains a minimum unrestricted liquidity reserve of exactly $1,400,000 and provides monthly financial reporting; he has not yet attached the analysis to the credit file.

PF2.text: Nadia found while reviewing the loan agreement this week that a covenant waiver may not exceed exactly 90 days and must include a no-new-debt covenant; this interpretation has not yet been circulated to underwriting.

PF3.text: Jonah received the borrower's signed funding letter yesterday confirming an equity injection of exactly $600,000 due within 15 calendar days, which makes the temporary waiver supportable; the letter is still in his client file and has not been uploaded to the credit system.

acceptance_conditions: The covenant waiver must be approved.
The waiver must last exactly 90 days.
The borrower must maintain exactly $1,400,000 of unrestricted liquidity.
The borrower must make exactly a $600,000 equity injection within 15 calendar days.
Monthly financial reporting must be required during the waiver.
A no-new-debt covenant must be included in the waiver.
The updated risk stress test must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: Without PF1, the reported ratio supports no exact liquidity floor or monthly reporting requirement, so a generic waiver would leave minimum_liquidity_reserve_usd at 0 and monthly_reporting_required false.

Without PF2, the borrower's requested 120-day waiver would remain the apparent term and no-new-debt covenant would be omitted, so waiver_days would not be 90 and no_new_debt_covenant_required would be false.

Without PF3, there is no confirmed source of support for approval, and the settlement would not specify the exact $600,000 equity injection due within 15 days or include its equity_injection commitment.
